Thermoelectric nanocoating enables remote fire warning in 2.1 s

Researchers have developed a flexible layered nanocoating combining thermoelectric graphene, PEDOT:PSS and an ionic liquid that delivers both flame retardancy and highly sensitive temperature sensing. The system enables remote real-time monitoring and triggers a fire warning within 2.1 s of flame exposure.

8 October 2026
Fire protective coatings Fire retardant coatings

Instaread

The rapid growth of flexible electronic devices has increased the demand for fire-safe materials that combine flame retardancy with early fire detection. The authors present a flexible nanocoating with a layered heterostructure prepared through the synergistic assembly of thermoelectric graphene (TEG), poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) and the ionic liquid 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium octyl sulfate. The design addresses a key limitation of organic thermoelectric materials: electronic-type systems offer rapid charge transport but low Seebeck coefficients, whereas ionic-type systems provide high Seebeck coefficients but suffer from slow ion kinetics and signal fluctuations.

By combining both carrier types within an ordered layered architecture, the coating achieves synchronous electron and ion transport. The ionic liquid further enhances this synergy, enabling precise and stable thermoelectric responses that overcome the typically incompatible structural requirements of electronic and ionic transport media.

Linear temperature-voltage response for early fire detection

Across the temperature range of 50–300 °C, the maximum output voltage of the nanocoating follows a stable linear relationship with contact temperature (Umax = 0.0197 T – 0.5583). This predictable response allowed the coating to be integrated with a wireless signal transmission module, enabling remote real-time temperature monitoring during the latent heating phase before ignition. When exposed to open flame, the system triggered a fire warning within only 2.1 s. The nanocoating also retained stable performance after repeated burn cycles, supporting its suitability for long-term fire-safety applications.

Flame retardancy for flexible substrates

In addition to its sensing function, the coating provided effective flame retardancy on flexible flammable substrates including polyester (PET) films and polyurethane (PU) foams. Treated materials achieved self-extinguishing behaviour in vertical burning tests and met the UL-94 V-0 classification. According to the authors, the combination of ion-electron synergistic thermoelectric response, layered heterostructure and flame-retardant performance offers a new strategy for improving the fire safety of flexible electronic materials and advancing IoT-integrated smart fire-protection systems.

Source: Liao, J. et al., A layered flexible nanocoating with ion-electron synergistic thermoelectric response for highly sensitive remote fire-warning. Progress in Organic Coatings, 110403 (2026).
